ISSUE:
Changelog drops merge commits

Our release branches are merged with merge commits whose subjects carry the pull request titles, for example `Merge pull request #41 from team/export`, and the generated changelog never lists them.

`CommitsCmd("v1.2.0", "HEAD")` builds:

    git log --no-merges --pretty=format:%s v1.2.0..HEAD

Expected:

    git log --pretty=format:%s v1.2.0..HEAD

so merge subjects become part of the changelog.

Preferred fix: stop passing `--no-merges` when listing the commits for the changelog. Filtering a second query afterwards would also work, but it doubles the git calls.


For reference, the fix changed these inputs the issue itself names:
CASE c1: issue example: commit subjects between v1.2.0 and HEAD
  before the fix: git log --no-merges --pretty=format:%s v1.2.0..HEAD
  after the fix:  git log --pretty=format:%s v1.2.0..HEAD
CASE c2: commit subjects between v1.0.0 and v1.1.0
  before the fix: git log --no-merges --pretty=format:%s v1.0.0..v1.1.0
  after the fix:  git log --pretty=format:%s v1.0.0..v1.1.0
CASE c3: argument count of the commit subjects command
  before the fix: 5
  after the fix:  4

Each case below printed one thing before the fix and another after it. For each case, decide whether the issue asks for that change:
- requested: the issue asks for it, or it follows directly and necessarily from what the issue asks.
- unrequested: the issue neither asks for it nor implies it; a maintainer would expect this output to stay as it was.
- unknown: the issue does not decide it.

CASE k1: authors command keeps --no-merges and author format
  before the fix: git log --no-merges --pretty=format:%an <%ae> v1.0.0..HEAD
  after the fix:  git log --pretty=format:%an <%ae> v1.0.0..HEAD

CASE k2: shared log prefix with a custom format
  before the fix: git log --no-merges --pretty=format:%H
  after the fix:  git log --pretty=format:%H

Answer one line per case: <case id>: requested|unrequested|unknown
